title: We Are South Maui: Community Plan Advisory Committee Meeting of April 26, 2023

issues.title: Harbor triangle rezoning including Maui Ocean Center

recap.headline: South Maui plan committee reviews land use categories and sets Māʻalaea map designations
recap.in_60_seconds: The South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee heard a Planning Department briefing on the 15 proposed land use designations, then worked on the Māʻalaea sub-area map. Five people testified, raising vague designation definitions, open space and water use in Māʻalaea, truck safety in ʻŌhukai, and wetland land near Keālia. The committee adopted residential for the Haʻoli Street condos without objection, rejecting a resort hotel request, and adopted the department's other Māʻalaea designations 9-1. A second vote to make the Māʻalaea triangle Small Town Center instead of Transit-Oriented Corridor was first announced as passing. Staff later said it fell one vote short of the seven needed, so the triangle must be revisited. Votes on the designation definitions and ahupuaʻa wording for the sub-area are set for next week.

parts.title: Opening and agenda
presented: Meeting opened at 5:30 p.m. with roll call.
Agenda: designations presentation, public testimony, then the Māʻalaea sub-area; no decisions on the designations tonight.
Akaka began a trial live broadcast, with remote testimony hoped for starting next week.

parts.title: Presentation on proposed community plan designations
parts.presenter: Long Range Division planner, Planning Department
presented: Community plan designations sit between the Maui Island Plan growth boundaries and zoning, a broad view rather than zoning.
15 designations, including 2 residential and 4 mixed-use types: rural village, neighborhood center, small town center and transit-oriented corridor.
Transit-oriented corridor is the densest mixed-use type, for example Wailuku Town; Dolphin Center is an example of small town center.
Ended with a quiz to help members learn the designations.

raised.concern: Designation definitions are too vague, and landowners could use them to justify unwanted projects; they should be tightened.
The Māʻalaea triangle does not fit transit-oriented corridor; Māʻalaea sees itself as a small town.
Māʻalaea needs more open space and less density, citing drainage and sewage problems; the roughly 250-acre mauka parcel should never be developed because it is fire prone and windy.
South Maui uses water taken from Wailuku while Wailuku residents face yearly restrictions; South Maui should conserve.
Industrial uses next to homes in ʻŌhukai bring big trucks that endanger children.
The plan should not rely on speculative developer plans.
Mākaʻi Mahi Pono land near Keālia Pond has become a campsite and should be managed with the National Wildlife Refuge.
The road at Keālia should be moved mauka of the wetland.

answered.said: The Planning Commission decided not to refer the ʻŌhukai matter to the South Maui Advisory Committee and will decide it itself.
The North Kīhei sub-area, which includes ʻŌhukai, will be covered next week.

next.what: Committee reviews North Kīhei sub-area, including ʻŌhukai

parts.title: Questions on designations and vision statement
presented: A member said a proposal for more specific designations is posted and will be taken up next week.
A member read the South Maui vision statement from page 29.

next.what: Discussion of a member's proposal for more specific designations

parts.title: Māʻalaea sub-area text and ahupuaʻa
presented: The chair named two issues: the triangle as transit-oriented corridor, and the Māʻalaea Village Association request to make Haʻoli Street condos resort hotel.
Members asked that the text name the Waikapū and Ukumehame ahupuaʻa and the historic Lahaina Pali Trail.
A member from Māʻalaea described a fragile ecosystem and lost cultural sites.

answered.said: The department will propose ahupuaʻa language next week for the committee to approve.

next.what: Planning Department proposes ahupuaʻa language for sub-area text

parts.title: Māʻalaea triangle designation
presented: The triangle is about 25 to 30 acres, including a roughly 10-acre parking lot; it is commercial in the 1998 plan.
Transit-oriented corridor maps to B2/B3 zoning, up to 140-foot buildings; small town center maps to B1/B2, up to 90 feet.
Some members cited wind, view corridor and parking concerns; others cited the need for affordable housing near jobs.

answered.said: The site already serves as a transit hub between parts of the island and could someday have apartments; a designation allows residential but does not mean it will happen.
If a motion fails, the department's proposed designation stands; view planes would be reviewed in an SMA permit.

parts.title: Haʻoli Street condominiums
presented: Most condos have apartment zoning but short-term rental status; the department proposed residential, keeping the status quo.
The Māʻalaea Village Association asked for resort hotel.

answered.said: Resort hotel would not change property taxes but could allow rezoning to hotel, removing the County's future option to return units to housing.

parts.title: Remaining Māʻalaea designations
presented: A member raised moving the road mauka of Keālia wetlands as a possible bypass.
Staff said there are no project districts proposed for South Maui; the old Project District 11 area becomes agriculture.
A member asked whether the harbor should be special purpose instead of employment center.

answered.said: Moving the road mauka is already covered by a policy and an action item in the plan.
The Small Town Center motion was not adopted because it needed seven votes of the full committee.

parts.title: Closing
presented: Meeting adjourned at 8:08 p.m.

moments.who: Planning Department Long Range Division staff
moments.quote: It's important to keep in mind that we are operating at the level of community plan designations, this 30,000 foot view, not zoning.
moments.about: Staff explained in 2023 that the South Maui Community Plan sets broad land use designations, not parcel zoning.

moments.who: a former member of the General Plan Advisory Committee
moments.quote: I'm not making up the plan. The person who owns the land is going to make up the plan.
moments.about: A testifier warned that vague designation definitions in the draft plan would let landowners decide what gets built.

moments.who: a former member of the General Plan Advisory Committee
moments.quote: I don't know anyone in Ma'alai'a that can meet the majority of their needs by going to that triangle unless you just like eating at one of the local restaurants or something.
moments.about: A testifier argued the Maʻalaea triangle around the Maui Ocean Center does not fit a transit-oriented designation.

moments.who: a South Maui resident speaking for Maui Tomorrow
moments.quote: And so, clarity of purpose for these designations, I think, is very, very important.
moments.about: Maui Tomorrow urged the advisory committee to tighten the wording of the plan's land use designations.

moments.who: a community plan advisory committee member
moments.quote: It's extremely windy there. That's a wind corridor. And it's a view corridor.
moments.about: A committee member opposed housing on the triangle because of wind and the ocean view from the highway.

moments.who: Planning Department Long Range Division staff
moments.quote: It does already serve as kind of a transit hub between all the parts of the island. So the possibility of having maybe some apartments there where people could have a shorter transit.
moments.about: Staff gave the reasoning for proposing a designation that allows residential use on the Maʻalaea triangle.

moments.who: the community plan advisory committee chair
moments.quote: And I think that the upside of that is that it recognizes the current use. The downside is that it means that that's where it will be forever.
moments.about: The chair weighed a request to designate the Haʻoli Street vacation-rental condos in Maʻalaea as resort hotel instead of residential.

moments.who: a community plan advisory committee member
moments.quote: They currently pay a hotel rate for the land underneath and short-term vacation rental for the individual units, unless they have a homeowner exemption or it's their permanent home.
moments.about: A committee member explained how the Maʻalaea apartment-zoned vacation rentals are taxed today.

moments.quote: You need seven votes because it has to be of the total quorum, not of the people present.
moments.about: Staff said the Small Town Center designation for the triangle was not actually adopted and would need to be revisited.
